transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. As part of our normal incident-review routine, I need to make sure our remediation plan is solid before I approve it. Right now the draft has the retry configuration change recorded as the immediate cause of the duplicate notifications during that 26-minute window on Tuesday. Before we finalize, I'd like to hear from both of you. First, to the on-call SRE: are there any findings from your investigation that should change our remediation plan?

transcript.text: Thanks, Riley. I'm ready to share my findings on the customer impact side as soon as it's my turn. I do have information that I think needs to be reflected in the remediation plan before it's finalized.

transcript.text: Riley, yes — I have a finding that should change the remediation plan. While tracing a separate timeout alert this morning, I found that the retry worker bypasses the payment provider's idempotency key on its timeout path. This means a future timeout can still create duplicate deliveries even if the retry configuration change is reverted. I haven't filed this in the incident tracker yet, but the remediation plan must include an idempotency-remediation commitment for the payment-webhook-retry-worker and a duplicate-delivery replay test that verifies the idempotency fix prevents duplicates under timeout conditions.

I hadn't updated the incident channel yet because I was waiting for the support ticket details to be reconciled.
